conventions.convention: The complex L² pairing is linear in its first argument: ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫f conjugate(g).
Weyl quantization uses phase exp(i(x−y)·ξ/ε), midpoint symbol a((x+y)/2,ξ), and factor (2πε)^(−d). The Wigner transform uses phase exp(−iy·ξ/ε) and the same factor.
The scaled Fourier transform has negative phase exp(−ix·ξ/ε) and factor (2πε)^(−d/2). The variables and ε are dimensionless.
The Poisson bracket is {a,b} = ∇x a·∇ξ b − ∇ξ a·∇x b; the first composition correction is +(iε/2){a,b}.
The evolution satisfies i∂t Uε = Hε Uε/ε. The Heisenberg observable Uε(t)* Op(a) Uε(t) corresponds to a composed with the forward Hamiltonian flow Φt.

The Egorov theorem assumes a self-adjoint extension with Schwartz space as a graph core; it does not derive that operator realization for every potential. Its nonquadratic estimate covers fixed finite times.
The semiclassical estimates explicitly assume Countable Choice and use 0 < ε ≤ 1; the initial definition and scaled Plancherel and kernel identities allow every ε > 0.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice, d ≥ 1 and 0 < ε ≤ 1. For smooth a on R^(2d) with bounded derivatives through N_d = 4d+4, the cross-Wigner form defines a unique bounded Weyl operator with norm at most C_d ∑_{|α|≤N_d} ‖∂^α a‖∞, uniformly in ε. For Schwartz symbols it agrees with the kernel definition.

Assume Countable Choice, d ≥ 1, 0 < ε ≤ 1, real smooth V with all derivatives of order at least two bounded, and a ∈ C_c^∞(R^(2d)). For h = |ξ|²/2 + V and Hε⁰ = −ε²Δ/2 + V on Schwartz space, (i/ε)[Hε⁰,Opε(a)] = Opε({a,h}) + ε²Opε(r), where r is smooth and ∑_{|α|≤4d+4} ‖∂^α r‖∞ ≤ C_{d,V} p_{12d+16}(a), uniformly in ε.

For d ≥ 1 and ε > 0, defines Schwartz Weyl quantization, the Wigner distribution of a normalized Schwartz vector, the scaled Fourier transform, and Q_j u = x_j u, P_j u = −iε∂_j u with [Q_j,P_k] = iεδ_jk on Schwartz space.

Under Countable Choice, the stated subquadratic-potential hypotheses and explicit self-adjoint-extension/Schwartz-core hypothesis, every compactly supported smooth symbol has a uniform O(ε²) Heisenberg-versus-classical transport error on each fixed finite time interval. The error vanishes for potentials of degree at most two. For every real quadratic phase-space Hamiltonian, under the separately stated self-adjoint/core hypothesis, exact covariance holds for all Schwartz symbols and all real times.

Assume Countable Choice, d ≥ 1, ε > 0, a ∈ S(R^(2d)), and normalized u ∈ S(R^d). Its Wigner distribution is real and integrable, pairs with a as ⟨Opε(a)u,u⟩, and has position and momentum marginals |u(x)|² and |Fεu(ξ)|². It need not be nonnegative.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let d ≥ 1, ε > 0, and define Fε on S(R^d) by def-nrqmx-weyl-symbol-wigner. It extends uniquely to a unitary operator on L²(R^d).

Under Countable Choice, for d ≥ 1, ε > 0 and Schwartz a, the Weyl kernel has L² norm (2πε)^(−d/2)‖a‖₂ and defines a bounded L² operator with norm at most that kernel norm, agreeing with the Schwartz-space definition.

Complex Lp classes, componentwise derivatives, and first-variable-linear pairing.
Coordinate product rules and the canonical commutator.
The explicitly adopted ACω hypothesis.
Unitary extension of the negative-sign, 2π-normalized Fourier transform.
Dilation norm identities, null-set invariance, kernel coordinates and translations.
Nonnegative kernel, packet and Schur-bound integrals.
Complex L² Hilbert structure for kernel bounds and form representation.
Kernel bounds, packet estimates, Schur estimates and uncertainty inequality.
Schwartz Fourier factors, partial transforms and Schwartz Weyl kernels.
Wigner marginals, Fourier-mode Weyl representation and remainder reconstruction.
Exchanging absolutely integrable Fourier, kernel and Taylor integrals.
Gaussian packet identities, normalization and explicit Wigner calculations.
Fourier decay, kernel commutators, Gaussian moments and oscillator symmetry.
Complex integrals under reflections, affine changes, frequency scaling and oscillator rotation.
Uniqueness and extension of bounded forms and Fourier-mode operator identities.
Representing the bounded cross-Wigner form by an L² operator, with the conjugations appropriate to the pairing convention.
Repeated interval integration of smooth scalar curves to derive Taylor remainders and potential growth bounds.
Smooth potential compositions, variational equations and transported-symbol derivatives.
Self-adjoint operator and closedness conventions in the Egorov domain argument.
Initial flow regularity and first two variational equations; higher regularity is developed locally.
Completeness and stability of the Hamiltonian flow when the potential gradient is globally Lipschitz.
Bounded Hessian implies globally Lipschitz potential gradient.
Finite-time flow derivative bounds and uniqueness of the affine quadratic flow.
Integrating strongly continuously differentiable L²-valued Heisenberg curves.
Unitary evolution preserving the graph domain for the constant self-adjoint generator H/ε.
Self-adjoint oscillator realization, eigenvalues, diagonal domain and finite-Hermite graph core.
Polynomial-Gaussian eigenfunctions and the explicit first excited state.
One-dimensional differentiation in the Gaussian oscillator verification.
Twice differentiating the Gaussian Fourier integral in the negative-Wigner counterexample.
